clips.title: Section 1: Registering at a health clinic

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Good morning, Northfield Health Clinic. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: Good morning. I have just moved to this area, and I would like to register with the clinic and see a doctor about my knee.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Of course. Could I take your full name first, please?

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: It is Daniel Mercer. Mercer is spelled M-E-R-C-E-R.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Thank you, Mr Mercer. And your date of birth?

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: The fourteenth of March, nineteen eighty-eight.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: And a contact phone number, please?

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: It is 0774, 221, 908. Oh, sorry, I said that wrong. The last three digits are 980, not 908.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: No problem, I have changed that. Now, what is the problem with your knee?

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: I have had a pain in my left knee for about three weeks, and it gets worse when I climb stairs.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Dr Patel has a free appointment on Tuesday at twenty past nine.

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: Tuesday morning is difficult, because I take my daughter to school and then go straight to work.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Let me check Thursday instead. There is a free slot at ten forty on Thursday morning with Dr Patel.

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: Thursday at ten forty is perfect, thank you.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Before that appointment, Dr Patel would like you to have a blood test, to check for inflammation.

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: Do I need to prepare for the blood test in any way?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Yes. You must not eat anything for eight hours before the test, although you can drink water.

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: And when will the blood test be?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: The laboratory opens at half past eight, and your test is booked for nine o'clock on Wednesday morning.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: The test normally costs twelve pounds, but patients who register today receive a discount of twenty-five per cent.

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: That is fine. How will I get the results?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: We will send the results by text message within three working days, and Dr Patel will discuss them with you on Thursday.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Please arrive ten minutes before your appointment, and bring some photo identification with you on the first visit.

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: Is there parking at the clinic? I usually drive to appointments.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: There is a small car park behind the building, and the first hour is free for patients.

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: And if my knee gets worse before Thursday, what should I do?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Call us straight away, and a nurse will phone you back to decide whether you need to come in earlier.

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: That is very helpful. One last thing: can I choose to see the same doctor each time?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: We try to book you with the same doctor whenever possible, so that your care stays consistent.

lines.speaker: Mr Mercer
lines.text: Thank you very much for your help.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: You are welcome, Mr Mercer. We look forward to seeing you on Wednesday for the blood test.

clips.title: Section 2: An open day at a distribution centre

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Welcome to the Northgate Distribution Centre, and thank you for joining one of our public open days.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: This is the largest of the company's five distribution centres, and it opened in twenty nineteen.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: The warehouse covers forty-five thousand square metres, roughly the size of six football pitches.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Around three hundred and twenty people work here, in shifts that cover twenty-four hours a day.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Every day, about sixty lorries arrive at the loading bays, bringing goods from ports and factories across the country.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Inside the warehouse, thirty-two robots move shelves to the packing stations, so staff no longer walk long distances.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: During the busiest periods, these robots can sort up to nine hundred parcels an hour.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Until last year, the centre handled about twelve thousand parcels a day, but that figure has now risen to fifteen thousand.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Before the tour begins, please put on the yellow jacket we give you, and stay with your guide at all times.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: For safety reasons, visitors are not allowed to take photographs in the robot zone.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Tours used to start at the main gate, but from this month, all tours start here at the visitor reception.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: The guided tour lasts ninety minutes, and it ends with a short film of twenty-five minutes about the history of the company.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: The normal price of the tour is ten pounds, but today, for the open day, every visitor receives a discount of twenty per cent.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: On the roof, you can see one thousand, two hundred solar panels, which provide a third of the centre's electricity.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: At the end of the tour, the cafe serves hot drinks and light meals, and it closes at half past five.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Finally, if you are interested in working here, application forms are available at the reception desk.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: The centre is open for public tours every Saturday, and school groups are welcome on weekdays by arrangement.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: A family ticket for two adults and two children costs twenty-five pounds on normal days, which is cheaper than buying separate tickets.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Visitors who arrive by train can take the free shuttle bus from Mill Road station, which leaves every thirty minutes.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: In the delivery yard, you can watch the lorries being loaded through the glass wall of the viewing platform.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Each lorry is checked by computer before it leaves, so the driver always takes the fastest route for that day.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: The centre also runs a training programme, and last year it trained forty new lorry drivers for the company.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Before you leave, please return your yellow jacket to the desk, and collect a printed visitor badge as a souvenir.

lines.speaker: Guide
lines.text: Tours for the afternoon begin at two o'clock, and booking online is strongly recommended at weekends.

clips.title: Section 3: Planning a research project on sleep and memory

lines.speaker: Tutor
lines.text: Come in, Mia and Tom. Let us talk about your research project on sleep and learning.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: We have decided to study how sleep affects students' memory before examinations.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: At first, we wanted to include all the students at the university, but that group is far too large for one project.

lines.speaker: Tutor
lines.text: I agree with you. You should narrow the group down. Why not focus on students who also have part-time jobs?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: That is a good suggestion, because those students often sleep fewer hours than other students.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Our first plan was to send a questionnaire to two hundred students, but in the end only one hundred and twenty returned it.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: So instead, we will ask thirty volunteers to keep a sleep diary for fourteen nights, spending about five minutes on each entry.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thirty diaries will give us detailed daily information, which the questionnaire could not provide.

lines.speaker: Tutor
lines.text: That sounds workable. But how will you measure memory itself?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Each morning, the volunteers will learn a list of twenty words, and in the evening they will try to recall as many as possible.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I am not sure interviews are a good idea, because they would take far too long to analyse.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I partly agree with you, Tom, but a few short interviews would help us explain the diary results.

lines.speaker: Tutor
lines.text: Then do both. Use the diaries as your main source of data, and add just four short interviews.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I will collect the diaries and the word-test scores every Friday.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: And I will present the results in charts, because I am quicker than Tom with the statistics software.

lines.speaker: Tutor
lines.text: One more thing. Your presentation was planned for the tenth of June, but the department has moved it to the seventeenth of June.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: That is good news. The change gives us an extra week to finish the analysis.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We also need to get permission from the ethics committee before we can start.

lines.speaker: Tutor
lines.text: Yes, that is essential. Submit the application form by Monday, and you can begin the following week.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Thank you, Dr Shah. We will send you the final plan by email tomorrow.

lines.speaker: Tutor
lines.text: Before you go, decide who will write each section of the report.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I will write the introduction and the results section, if that is all right with Tom.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Yes, and I will describe the method and keep a record of every meeting we have.

lines.speaker: Tutor
lines.text: Good. You can also book one of the small study rooms in the library for your Friday meetings.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: How long should the final report be?

lines.speaker: Tutor
lines.text: About three thousand words, not counting the charts or the diary extracts in the appendix.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: We will book the room for Friday and start designing the diary page this week.

clips.title: Section 4: A lecture on the history of food preservation

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: In this lecture, I will trace the development of food preservation, from the earliest drying racks to the freezers of today.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: The oldest method of all is drying. In hot, dry regions, people spread meat, fish and fruit in the sun, removing the water that bacteria need in order to grow.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Salting was equally important in the ancient world, because salt draws water out of food and creates conditions in which most bacteria cannot survive.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Salted fish could be traded over long distances, so reliable supplies of salt became extremely valuable to ancient markets.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: A third ancient technique is fermentation, in which useful bacteria or yeasts change the food itself and protect it from harmful organisms.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: For centuries, wealthy households also stored ice, cut from frozen lakes in winter, in deep pits lined with straw.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: A major change came in eighteen hundred and nine, when a French cook, Nicolas Appert, won a government prize for preserving food in sealed glass bottles heated in water.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Only a year later, in England, Peter Durand patented the tin can, which was stronger than glass but far more difficult to open.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: At that time, nobody understood why heating preserved food, because the role of bacteria in spoiling food was still unknown.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: The explanation came in the eighteen sixties, when Louis Pasteur showed that gentle heating killed the bacteria that spoiled wine.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: His method, now known as pasteurisation, was soon applied to milk, and it greatly reduced the spread of disease through milk.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Mechanical refrigeration spread during the late nineteenth century, and it allowed ships to carry frozen meat between continents.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: In the nineteen twenties, Clarence Birdseye developed quick freezing, which preserved the texture of fish and vegetables far better than slow freezing had done.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Finally, freeze-drying, which removes water from already frozen food, became common in the middle of the twentieth century, first for medicines and later for instant coffee.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Each method, then, rests on the same simple principle: bacteria must be stopped from growing, whether by removing water, adding salt, heating or cooling the food.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: The nineteenth century also saw a huge international trade in natural ice, which was cut in North America and shipped as far as India.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: The ice was packed in sawdust to slow the melting, and a surprising share of each cargo still arrived in usable condition.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Today, of course, most preserved food relies on a combination of methods rather than a single one.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: A ready meal, for example, may be cooked, sealed without air, and then kept at a low temperature throughout its journey to the shop.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Understanding these older techniques is still useful, because they show how each generation solved the same problem with the materials it had.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Next week, we will turn to the modern cold chain, and to the energy costs of keeping food cold from factory to table.

items.stem: When will the students give their presentation?

explanation.whyCorrect: Buổi thuyết trình đã được khoa dời sang ngày mười bảy tháng Sáu.
explanation.whyWrong: Ngày mười là kế hoạch cũ; thứ Hai là hạn nộp đơn đạo đức và ngày mai là hạn gửi kế hoạch.
explanation.trap: Phải lấy ngày sau khi khoa thay đổi lịch, không lấy ngày dự kiến ban đầu.

evidence.quote: the department has moved it to the seventeenth of June

items.stem: The students need permission from the {{1}} committee before they start.

explanation.whyCorrect: Nhóm phải xin phép ủy ban đạo đức trước khi bắt đầu thu thập dữ liệu.

evidence.quote: get permission from the ethics committee
get permission from the ethics committee

items.stem: The oldest method of preserving food is {{1}}.

explanation.whyCorrect: Phơi khô là phương pháp bảo quản thực phẩm lâu đời nhất mà bài giảng nêu.

evidence.quote: The oldest method of all is drying
The oldest method of all is drying

items.stem: Salt preserves food because it draws {{1}} out of the food.

explanation.whyCorrect: Muối rút nước ra khỏi thực phẩm, khiến hầu hết vi khuẩn không thể sống sót.

evidence.quote: salt draws water out of food
salt draws water out of food

items.stem: Why did salt become extremely valuable in ancient markets?

explanation.whyCorrect: Cá muối có thể buôn bán qua quãng đường dài nên muối trở nên rất có giá trị.
explanation.whyWrong: Bài giảng không nói muối là cách duy nhất để ướp thịt; băng trong hố thuộc về các hộ giàu, không liên quan muối.

options.text: It was used to preserve ice.
Salted fish could be traded over long distances.
It was the only way to preserve meat.
Wealthy households used it in their ice pits.

evidence.quote: Salted fish could be traded over long distances

items.stem: In fermentation, useful bacteria or {{1}} change the food.

explanation.whyCorrect: Trong lên men, vi khuẩn có lợi hoặc nấm men làm biến đổi và bảo vệ thực phẩm.

evidence.quote: useful bacteria or yeasts change the food
useful bacteria or yeasts change the food

items.stem: Where was ice stored by wealthy households?

explanation.whyCorrect: Các hộ giàu trữ băng trong những hố sâu lót rơm sau khi cắt băng từ hồ đóng băng.
explanation.whyWrong: Hồ là nơi cắt băng chứ không phải nơi trữ; chai thủy tinh và lon thiếc thuộc về giai đoạn sau.

options.text: in deep pits lined with straw

evidence.quote: stored ice, cut from frozen lakes in winter, in deep pits lined with straw

items.stem: Year in which Appert won the government prize: {{1}}

explanation.whyCorrect: Nicolas Appert giành giải thưởng của chính phủ vào năm 1809 nhờ chai thủy tinh đậy kín đun trong nước.

evidence.quote: in eighteen hundred and nine, when a French cook, Nicolas Appert, won a government prize
in eighteen hundred and nine, when a French cook, Nicolas Appert, won a government prize

items.stem: What disadvantage did the tin can have, compared with glass bottles?

explanation.whyCorrect: Lon thiếc bền hơn chai thủy tinh nhưng khó mở hơn nhiều, đó là nhược điểm được nêu.
explanation.whyWrong: Lon thiếc không yếu hơn thủy tinh; bài giảng không nói lon không đun được hay bảo quản kém hơn.

options.text: It could not be heated in water.
It preserved food for a shorter time.
It was far more difficult to open.

evidence.quote: stronger than glass but far more difficult to open

items.stem: Pasteur showed that gentle heating killed the {{1}} that spoiled wine.

explanation.whyCorrect: Pasteur chứng minh đun nóng nhẹ tiêu diệt vi khuẩn làm hỏng rượu vang.

evidence.quote: gentle heating killed the bacteria that spoiled wine
gentle heating killed the bacteria that spoiled wine

items.stem: What was the main advantage of quick freezing over slow freezing?

explanation.whyCorrect: Cấp đông nhanh giữ được kết cấu của cá và rau tốt hơn hẳn cấp đông chậm.
explanation.whyWrong: Vận chuyển thịt bằng tàu và giảm bệnh qua sữa thuộc về tủ lạnh cơ học và thanh trùng, không phải cấp đông nhanh.

options.text: It made frozen food cheaper to transport.
It allowed ships to carry meat between continents.
It preserved the texture of food much better.
It reduced diseases carried in milk.

evidence.quote: quick freezing, which preserved the texture of fish and vegetables far better than slow freezing

items.stem: What principle lies behind all the methods described?

explanation.whyCorrect: Mọi phương pháp đều dựa trên một nguyên tắc chung: ngăn vi khuẩn phát triển.
explanation.whyWrong: Rút nước, đun nóng hay làm lạnh chỉ là từng cách riêng lẻ; không phương pháp nào áp dụng cho mọi trường hợp.

options.text: Bacteria must be stopped from growing.
All food must be heated before storage.
Water must be removed from all food.
Food must be kept as cold as possible.

evidence.quote: bacteria must be stopped from growing
